pluss::series::ones¶

Back to Series Factory API Reference

Signature¶

pluss::series::ones(sizes,
                    ScalarType dt = ScalarType::Float32) -> Series

pluss::series::ones(sizes,
                    Config cfg) -> Series

pluss::series::ones(sizes,
                    opts...) -> Series

pluss::series::ones(sizes,
                    {{"key", value}, ...}) -> Series

What It Builds¶

Allocates a new series and initializes every element to 1.

This is the unit-constant sibling of:

  • zeros()

  • full()

Use it when the constant value really is conceptually “one” rather than just “some repeated fill.”

Parameters¶

sizes

The requested output shape.

dt (ScalarType)

The explicit output dtype for the simple overload.

cfg (Config)

The config-based routing/dtype surface.

Returns¶

Series A newly allocated series filled entirely with ones.

Examples¶

Example 1. The default path emits a float32 tensor of ones.

std::cout << pluss::series::ones({2, 3});

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float32, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 1, 1],
  [1, 1, 1]]

Example 2. The dtype overload applies equally well to integer outputs.

std::cout << pluss::series::ones({4}, pluss::ScalarType::Int16);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int16, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1, 1, 1]

Notes¶

  • ones() is just the constant-1 specialization of the broader shape-first constructor family.

  • When the value is not literally one, prefer full().

See Also¶

  • pluss::series::zeros: the zero-valued sibling.

  • pluss::series::full: the general repeated-fill constructor.
